s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic musculoskeletal pain and stress fractures with abnormal bone mineralization
salient_findings: Stress fractures of the left rib, left sacrum, and left femoral neck
Abnormal bone densitometry with Z-scores of −2.5 in the lumbar spine and −1.9 in the femoral neck
key_facts: 2-year history of hip pain following low-impact falls
Elevated alkaline phosphatase level of 220 U/L
Fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) level of 1241 RU/mL
Bone densitometry showed Z-scores of −2.5 in the lumbar spine and −1.9 in the femoral neck
Genetic evaluation for hypophosphatemic disorders was unremarkable
Family history was negative for bone disease

shortlist.label: Hypophosphatemic rickets
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal bone mineralization and low phosphorus levels

shortlist.label: Osteomalacia
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated alkaline phosphatase and low 25-OH vitamin D levels

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Stress fractures and abnormal bone mineralization

raw.rationale: The patient's elevated FGF23 level of 1241 RU/mL, which is significantly above the normal range, is a key indicator of phosphatonin-related bone disease. This condition is characterized by high levels of FGF23, leading to hypophosphatemia, osteomalacia, and bone pain, all of which are present in this patient.

rejected.label: X-linked hypophosphatemia
rejected.why: Genetic evaluation was unremarkable, making this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Hypophosphatemic rickets
rejected.why: While the patient has hypophosphatemia, the presence of significantly elevated FGF23 levels points more towards phosphatonin-related bone disease

rejected.label: Osteomalacia
rejected.why: While the patient has features of osteomalacia, the underlying cause appears to be related to the elevated FGF23 levels, making phosphatonin-related bone disease a more specific diagnosis

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: The presence of a single intracortical lesion on the gallium-68 DOTATATE PET/MRI is not sufficient to diagnose fibrous dysplasia, especially given the other biochemical and clinical findings
